newsitem.title: INDIA: India transfers more powers to market regulator.
newsitem.headline: India transfers more powers to market regulator.

text.p: The Indian government on Monday transferred more powers to the domestic market regulator Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) to strengthen its grip over the stock markets, an official statement said.
"The main objective of these amendments is to further strengthen the regulatory powers of SEBI over the securities market," it said.

SEBI will now take decisions relating to recognition of stock exchanges, qualifications for memberships of exchanges, disciplinary actions against members, submission of annual report and requirements regarding listing of stocks.
The federal government also appointed Jayant Rama Varma as a part-time member of SEBI.
"The appointment will take effect from the date he assumes charge," it said.
Varma teaches at Indian Institute of Management, Ahmedabad, it added.
